summary: Ludwig Ross was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kiel University (~1825–1827). He held posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).

Ludwig Sütterlin was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig and earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University under Hermann Osthoff. He held posts at Heidelberg (PD in 1890, ao. Professor 1896–1913) and Freiburg (chair, 1913–1924).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Owens College, TU Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge (Ph.D. ~1929). He held positions at Trinity College and was a philosophy professor at Cambridge (1930–1947).

Indologist Ludwik Skurzak studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak, in Paris under Louis Renou, Jean Przyluski, and Jules Bloch, and under Helena Willman-Grabowska and Stanisław Schayer. He served as professor at the University of Breslau (1945–1978).

Ludwik Sternbach was an Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University under Helena Willman-Grabowska and Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak. He held posts at Jagiellonian, Lviv, Mumbai, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and was Honorary Professor at Collège de France (1972–1976).

Luigi Heilmann worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Padua under Luigi Suali and Ambrogio Ballini, and later at Bologna. His career included posts at Università Cattolica, Pavia, Cagliari, and Bologna (ordinary professor ~1956–1981).
Luigi Pio Tessitori was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini from ~1906 to 1910.

Luigi Suali was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Bologna under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bologna (1907) and the University of Pavia (1909–1910, and ord. Professor 1914–1956).

Luigia Nitti-Dolci was an Indologist and linguist who earned her doctorate at the University of Paris (~1928–1938), studying under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Theodor Bloch. She served at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (~1930–1939).

Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees at Puerto Rico, Yale (under Stanley Insler), and Michigan. He served as professor and department chair at the University of Michigan and was Academic Director at Mangalam Research Center.

Luise Hercus worked in Indology and linguistics. She studied at St Anne's College, Oxford, and the Australian National University. She taught at St Anne's (1948–1954), Adelaide (1965–1969), and the Australian National University (~1969–1991).

Luise Hilgenberg was an Indology scholar who earned both her Dr.med. (~1918–1922) and Dr. phil. (~1927–1933) at the University of Bonn, completing the latter under doctoral supervisor Willibald Kirfel.

Lumír Jisl worked in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Charles University (1940–1949), where he later became PD in 1960, and served as secretary at the CAS Institute of Archaeology in Prague in 1956.

Lungten Dubgyur is a scholar of Tibetology and law. He completed a graduate degree at Sherubtse College, earned an LL.B from Government Law College, Mumbai, and obtained an LL.M from the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso, earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery, and founded Menri Monastery, where he served as abbot beginning in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who earned his doctorate at Heidelberg University (~1965–1971) and his Habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin (-1986). He served as ordinary professor at the University of Cologne from 1989 to 2008.
Lyne Bansat-Boudon works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied under Armand Minard and Marie-Claude Porcher.

Lynette Monteiro works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa (1986–1996) and held positions at Sea Glass Psychological Services (1997) and the Ottawa Mindfulness Clinic (2003).

Lynn Struve is a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan (~1968–1974), and held an academic post at Indiana University Bloomington (~1977–2011).
